newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Low Australia inflation points to rate cut - Oppn.
newsitem.headline: Low Australia inflation points to rate cut - Oppn.

text.p: Australian acting opposition leader Gareth Evans said on Wednesday the Reserve Bank of Australia should cut interest rates again after June quarter data showed underlying inflation at a record low.
"There is every reason for the Reserve Bank to make another interest rate cut," Evans said in a statement.
"We can never say inflation is dead, but it is certainly dormant."
Evans said reducing official cash rates before the end of the week would not threaten the bank's annual underlying inflation target band of two to three percent.
"The bank must not squander this golden opportunity to boost growth by cutting interest rates one more time," Evans said.
Underlying inflation rose 0.3 percent in the June quarter for an annual rate of 1.7 percent, the lowest annual underlying inflation rate since the annual data started in 1972.
"If the economy was growing strongly and creating jobs, these figures would be tremendous news," Evans said.
"But today's extremely low inflation rate reflects the sluggish economy (Prime Minister John) Howard's government has delivered."
The Reserve Bank has eased monetary policy four times in the past year, cutting rates by 0.5 percentage points each time. Official cash rates currently stand at 5.5 percent.
The first rate cut was in July last year, while the most recent was on May 23.
